info.name: Consiva - Purpose Classifier (Agent 6 / DPC)
info.description:
API contract for the Purpose Classifier agent, covering all 7 endpoints defined in backend/app/api/v1/routes/purpose.py. Built entirely from static code reading (route handlers, purpose_run_service.py, db/models.py, core/exceptions.py, main.py exception handlers). NOT executed against any live server -- see the collection-level 'NOT VERIFIED' note below and the task report for what a human must do before running this for real.

Auth: person-JWT only, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (fastapi.security.HTTPBearer, see app/core/security.py get_current_user). Org scope is bound centrally by `bind_request_scope` in app/api/v1/router.py for every v1 route -- there is no per-route scope parameter.

Error envelope: Purpose does NOT use the `{"error": {"code":...}}` envelope that app/main.py reserves for paths starting with `/api/v1/consent-agent`. Every Purpose error -- including FastAPI's own 422 validation errors -- comes back as plain `{"detail": ...}` (app/main.py consiva_error_handler / validation_error_handler, the non-consent-agent branches). For a ConsivaError, `detail` is a string. For a framework RequestValidationError (bad body/query/path shape), `detail` is FastAPI's default list of `{loc, msg, type}` objects, NOT a string.

NOT VERIFIED LIVE: no request in this collection has been executed. To actually run it: point `baseUrl` at a non-production test deployment (never the prod docker-compose stack on this box), obtain a real bearer token (e.g. a non-production `/api/v1/dev/demo-token` if `AUTO_LOGIN_ENABLED`/development env, or a real login), and replace the placeholder `scanId`/`runId`/`findingId`/`foreignRunId`/`foreignFindingId` variables with real org-scoped IDs from that environment.

item.name: Happy path - queue assessment over a consent scan

request.description: CREATES STATE: inserts a new `purpose_runs` row (status=queued) and enqueues a `purpose_assessment` job (purpose_run_service.request_assessment, purpose.py:141-156). Re-running creates ANOTHER run every time -- this endpoint is not idempotent at the API layer (the `_mark_running` guard in purpose_run_service.py:244-288 only prevents the SAME run_id from being executed twice by the worker if its queued job is delivered more than once; it does nothing to stop two separate POSTs from creating two separate runs). Cleanup: delete/ignore the extra `purpose_runs` row if re-run against a real DB. Requires `scan_id` to reference a completed consent scan owned by the caller's org (ConsentScan.org_id == token org_id), else 404.

item.name: Backend quirk - invalid connector value returns 500, not 422

request.description: DOCUMENTED QUIRK, SAFE / no state created: `connector` is typed as a plain `str` on AssessSourceRequest (purpose.py:49), not a Pydantic Literal/enum, so an invalid value is NOT caught by request validation. It is only checked inside purpose_run_service.request_source_assessment (purpose_run_service.py:55-58), which raises the BASE `ConsivaError` (no subclass) for an unsupported connector. `ConsivaError.status_code` defaults to 500 (app/core/exceptions.py), so this comes back as a 500 Internal Server Error with `{"detail": "Unsupported connector 'mongodb'. Use 'postgres', 'csv' or 'rest'."}` -- a client-input error surfaced as a server error. Flagged in the final report as a likely bug (compare to e.g. InvalidUrlError=400 used elsewhere in exceptions.py for exactly this kind of shape problem).

exec: pm.test('status is 500 (documented quirk, NOT the semantically correct 400/422)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(500));
pm.test('detail names the bad connector', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.match(/Unsupported connector/));

item.name: Backend quirk - cross-org run_id returns 200 with empty list, not 404

request.description: CROSS-ORG TEST + DOCUMENTED INCONSISTENCY: unlike GET /assessments/{id} (endpoint 4), this handler never checks that `run_id` itself exists or belongs to the caller's org -- it only filters PurposeAssessment rows by `run_id` AND `org_id = caller_org` (purpose.py:230-236). For a run_id belonging to another org (or a run_id that doesn't exist at all), there are zero matching assessment rows under the caller's org, so the response is 200 with `[]`, NOT 404. A client cannot tell 'this run has no results yet' apart from 'this run_id belongs to someone else' apart from 'this run_id never existed' from this endpoint alone. READ-ONLY, safe to re-run.

exec: pm.test('status is 200 (not 404 -- documented inconsistency vs endpoint 4)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

CREATES/MUTATES STATE: overwrites `purpose_findings.status`, `decided_by_user_id`, `decided_at`, `decision_reason` for this finding and writes an audit_log row (purpose.py:290-303). NOT idempotent in a conflict-safe sense -- unlike the FindingAlreadyDecidedError pattern used elsewhere in this codebase (app/services/review_service.py), this handler never checks that the finding is still 'pending' before overwriting it, so calling it twice (even with different decisions) just silently overwrites the previous decision rather than returning 409. Cleanup before re-running against a real DB: reset the finding's status back to 'pending' or use a fresh findingId. Note the response model (FindingResponse) does NOT echo back decided_at/decided_by_user_id/decision_reason -- only id/assessment_id/finding_type/severity/title/description/review_required/status/created_at.
CREATES/MUTATES STATE -- see the approve request's description for the overwrite/cleanup caveat. `reason` is required for `rejected`/`dismissed` (enforced in the handler, purpose.py:274-279).

item.name: Backend quirk - reject without reason returns 500, not 422

request.description: DOCUMENTED QUIRK, SAFE / no state mutated (the finding lookup and write happen AFTER this check, purpose.py:272-288). purpose.py:274-279 raises the BASE `ConsivaError` (not the existing `ReasonRequiredError`, which is status_code=422 and used for exactly this situation elsewhere in app/services/review_service.py) when `decision` is rejected/dismissed and `reason` is blank. Base ConsivaError defaults to status_code=500 (app/core/exceptions.py), so a missing-reason request -- a plain client input error -- comes back as a 500 Internal Server Error: `{"detail": "A reason is required to reject a finding."}`. Flagged in the final report as a likely bug: this endpoint does not reuse the ReasonRequiredError convention already established for the same rule on other findings.

exec: pm.test('status is 500 (documented quirk, should likely be 422)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(500));
pm.test('detail mentions reason required', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.match(/reason is required/i));

item.name: Backend quirk - unknown decision value returns 404, not 422

request.description: DOCUMENTED QUIRK, SAFE / no state mutated. `decision` is typed as a plain `str` on DecisionRequest (purpose.py:125), not a Literal/enum, so Pydantic accepts any string. purpose.py:272-273 then validates it manually and raises `NotFoundError` -- the 404 exception class -- for an unrecognised value: `{"detail": "Unknown decision 'maybe'"}`. Using NotFoundError (404) for what is really an invalid-input/enum problem is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's HTTP semantics (compare InvalidEditError=422 in app/core/exceptions.py for an analogous out-of-enum value elsewhere). Flagged in the final report.

exec: pm.test('status is 404 (documented quirk, should likely be 422)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));
